summary: Raising the latte price from $5.00 to $5.50 decreased revenue by $28.25 despite slightly lower walkouts. Visits dropped 13 from 89 to 76, and espresso orders fell 4 while americano orders dropped 3, suggesting customers switched to cheaper alternatives rather than buying the higher-priced latte. Bagel orders surged 6 units, indicating a shift toward food items or lower-cost beverages. Wait time improved by 2.5 minutes as fewer customers crowded the shop, yet satisfaction remained flat at 3. Students were the hardest hit, losing $11.5 in revenue, while office workers declined only $5, showing price sensitivity varies by segment.
